source_text: καιροὺς ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Πατρὸς αὐτῶν,» τίς ἔσται λοιπὸν ἡ αὐτοῦ δόξα Χριστοῦ; Πῶς δὲ οὐ νοῦ καὶ λόγου πέρα παντὸς ἡ ἔκλαμψις; Χρυσοῖ δὲ τὴν κιβωτὸν ἔχοντες ἀναφορεῖς, χρυσοῖ καὶ οἱ κρίκοι, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ· μέτοχοι γὰρ τῆς δόξης οἱ ἀμφ' αὐτὸν, καὶ ὡς ἐν ἀγάπῃ καὶ ἁγιασμῷ προσερηρεισμένοι καὶ χρήσιμοι. Τοιοῦτοί τινες ἦσαν καὶ οἱ μακάριοι μαθηταὶ, δύναμιν τὴν παρ' αὐτοῦ τὴν θεοπρεπῆ δεχόμενοι, καὶ τῆς ἄνωθεν ὑπεροχῆς τὴν λαμπρότητα μεθεκτῶς ἐκπεπλουτηκότες, καὶ πληροῦντες διὰ τοῦτο τὰς θεοσημίας. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} «Καὶ πρός γε τῇ κιβωτῷ, ποιήσεις,» φησὶν, «ἱλαστήριον, ἐπίθεμα χρυσίου καθαροῦ δύο πήχεων καὶ ἡμίσους τὸ μῆκος, καὶ πήχεως καὶ ἡμίσους τὸ πλάτος. Καὶ ποιήσεις δύο Χερουβὶμ χρυσᾶ τορνευτά· καὶ ἐπιθήσεις αὐτὰ ἐξ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν κλιτῶν τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου. Ποιηθήσονται Χερουβὶμ εἷς ἐκ τοῦ κλίτους τούτου, καὶ Χερουβὶμ εἷς ἐκ τοῦ κλίτους τοῦ δευτέρου τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου. Καὶ ποιήσεις τοὺς δύο Χερουβὶμ ἐπὶ τὰ δύο κλίτη. Ἔσονται οἱ Χερουβὶμ ἐκτείνοντες τὰς πτέρυγας ἐπάνωθεν συσκιάζοντες ταῖς πτέρυξιν αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου, καὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν εἰσάλληλα, εἰς τὸ ἱλαστήριον ἔσονται τὰ πρόσωπα τῶν Χερουβίμ. Καὶ ἐπιθήσεις τὸ ἱλαστήριον ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν ἄνωθεν, καὶ εἰς τὴν κιβωτὸν ἐμβαλεῖς τὰ μαρτύρια ἃ ἂν δῶ σοι. Καὶ γνωσθήσομαί σοι ἐκεῖθεν, καὶ λαλήσω σοι ἄνωθεν τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν δύο Χερουβὶμ τῶν ὄντων ἐπὶ τῆς κιβωτοῦ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, κατὰ πάντα ὅσα ἂν ἐντείλωμαί σοι πρὸς τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εἶτα τί τὸ ἱλαστήριον εἶναι φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Ὅσον μὲν ἧκεν εἴς τε γράμμα καὶ σκιὰν, ἐκ χρυσοῦ ἐπεποίητο καθαροῦ, καὶ ἐπήρτητό πως ἐπικειμένη τῇ κιβωτῷ· εἴρηται γὰρ ἐπίθεμα διὰ τοῦτο. Τετραμμένοι δὲ εἰς αὐτὸ καὶ βλέποντες, οἱ τοῖς τῆς ἱερωσύνης αὐχήμασι κατηγλαϊσμένοι, πρὸς Θεὸν ἐδόκουν τετράφθαι καὶ βλέπειν. Φαμὲν δὲ εἶναι τὸ ἱλαστήριον, εἰ νοοῖτο πνευματικῶς, τὸν δι' ἡμᾶς γενόμενον ἄνθρωπον, «ὃν προέθετο ὁ Θεὸς ἱλαστήριον διὰ πίστεως ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ αἵματι, εἰς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ.» Παῦλος γὰρ ὧδέ φησιν. Ἐπιστέλλει δὲ ἡμῖν καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ σοφώτατος μαθητής· «Τεκνία, ταῦτα γράφω ὑμῖν, ἵνα μὴ ἁμάρτητε, καὶ ἐάν τις δὲ ἁμάρτῃ, παράκλητον ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα, Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν δίκαιον, καὶ αὐτὸς ἱλασμός ἐστι περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν, οὐ περὶ τῶν ἡμετέρων δὲ μόνων, ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ ὅλου τοῦ κόσμου.» Δι' αὐτοῦ γὰρ ἱλασμὸς, εὐχή τε πᾶσα, καὶ αἴτησις ἀγαθῶν. «Ἕως γὰρ ἄρτι,» φησὶν, «οὐκ ᾐτήσατε οὐδὲν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου· αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν.» Αὐτὸς οὖν ἄρα τὸ ἱλαστήριον. Δι' αὐτοῦ γὰρ ἡμῖν ἵλεως ὁ Πατὴρ, καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν καταλήγει πᾶν πέρας εὐχῆς, καὶ δι' αὐτοῦ πρόσιμεν, οὐχ ἑτέρως ὄντες δεκτοί. pass_a_gloss: [cont. Matthew 13:43 from s6: 'the righteous in due] times (κατὰ καιρούς) will shine out (ἐκλάμπω) as the sun in the kingdom of their Father,' what then will be the glory (δόξα) of Christ himself? How is the shining-out (ἔκλαμψις) not beyond all mind and word (νοῦ καὶ λόγου πέρα)? Gold are the poles (ἀναφορεῖς) that have/carry the ark, gold the rings (κρίκοι), and all things on it; for those around him (οἱ ἀμφ' αὐτόν) are sharers of the glory (μέτοχοι τῆς δόξης), as fastened/propped against him (προσερείδω, pf. pass.) in love and sanctification (ἀγάπη, ἁγιασμός), and useful (χρήσιμοι). Such were the blessed disciples, receiving from him the God-befitting power (δύναμις θεοπρεπής), and enriched (ἐκπλουτέω) by participation (μεθεκτῶς) with the brightness of the excellence from above (ἄνωθεν ὑπεροχή), and therefore fulfilling divine signs (θεοσημίαι). PALL: Rightly said. CYR: [Exodus 25:17–22 LXX] 'And besides the ark you will make a mercy seat (ἱλαστήριον), a cover (ἐπίθεμα) of pure gold, two and a half cubits long, one and a half wide. And you will make two cherubim of gold, turned/wrought (τορνευτά), and set them at both sides/ends (κλίτη) of the mercy seat. One cherub from this side, one from the second side. Make the two cherubim on the two sides. The cherubim will spread their wings above, overshadowing (συσκιάζω) the mercy seat with their wings, faces toward each other; toward the mercy seat will be the faces. And you will set the mercy seat on the head/top (ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλήν) above, and into the ark put the testimonies I give you. And I will be made known (γνωσθήσομαι) to you from there, and speak to you from above the mercy seat between the two cherubim on the ark of the testimony, about all I command you for the sons of Israel.' PALL: Then what do you say the mercy seat is? CYR: As far as reached into letter and shadow (γράμμα, σκιά), it was made of pure gold, and was somehow fitted (ἐπαρτάω), lying upon (ἐπίκειμαι) the ark; therefore called cover (ἐπίθεμα). Turned to it and looking, those adorned (καταγλαΐζω) with the boasts/honours (αὐχήματα) of priesthood (ἱερωσύνη) seemed (ἐδόκουν) to be turned toward God and looking. We say the mercy seat, understood spiritually (πνευματικῶς), is the one who became man for us (τὸν δι' ἡμᾶς γενόμενον ἄνθρωπον), 'whom God set forth (προτίθημι) as mercy seat through faith in his blood, for a showing (ἔνδειξις) of his righteousness (δικαιοσύνη).' Paul says so. John the wisest disciple writes: 'Little children ... we have an advocate (παράκλητος) with the Father, Jesus Christ righteous, and he is propitiation (ἱλασμός) for our sins, not ours only but of the whole world.' Through him propitiation, every prayer (εὐχή), and request (αἴτησις) of good things. 'Until now you asked nothing in my name; ask and it will be given you.' He then is the mercy seat. Through him the Father is gracious (ἵλεως) to us, and every end of prayer terminates (καταλήγει) in him, and through him we approach (πρόσειμι), not otherwise being acceptable (δεκτοί). Therefore he says, 'I am the way' and 'I am door (θύρα)' and 'No one comes to the' [cont. in s8].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …time will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father’ (Matthew 13:43), what then will the glory of Christ himself be? And how can his radiance not pass beyond all thought and speech? The poles that carry the ark are gold, the rings are gold too, and so is everything on it; for those around him share in his glory, since they are, as it were, fastened to him in love and sanctification, and are of use. Such, too, were the blessed disciples, who received from him the power that befits God, grew rich, by participation, in the brightness of the supreme excellence that comes from above, and for this reason worked divine signs.

Cyril: ‘And besides the ark,’ he says, ‘you shall make a mercy seat, a cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide. And you shall make two cherubim of wrought gold, and set them at the two ends of the mercy seat. One cherub shall be made at this end, and one cherub at the other end of the mercy seat; and you shall make the two cherubim at the two ends. The cherubim shall spread out their wings above, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces shall be toward one another; the faces of the cherubim shall be toward the mercy seat. And you shall set the mercy seat on the top, above, and into the ark you shall put the testimonies that I will give you. And I will make myself known to you from there, and I will speak to you from above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim that are on the ark of the testimony, about everything that I command you for the sons of Israel’ (Exodus 25:17–22).
Palladius: Then what do you say the mercy seat is?

Cyril: As far as the letter and the shadow go, it was made of pure gold, and was in some way fitted on, lying upon the ark; that is why it is called a cover. And those adorned with the honors of the priesthood, when they turned toward it and looked at it, were held to be turning toward God and looking at him. But we say that the mercy seat, if it is understood spiritually, is he who became man for our sake, ‘whom God put forward as a mercy seat through faith, in his blood, to show his righteousness’ (Romans 3:25). For so Paul says. And John, the wisest disciple, also writes to us: ‘Little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous; and he is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the whole world’ (1 John 2:1–2). For through him come propitiation, every prayer, and the asking of good things. For ‘until now,’ he says, ‘you have asked nothing in my name (John 16:24); ask, and it will be given to you’ (Matthew 7:7). So he himself is the mercy seat. For through him the Father is gracious to us; in him every prayer reaches its end; and through him we draw near, since in no other way are we acceptable. choices.why: ἱλαστήριον is rendered 'mercy seat' throughout, including in Romans 3:25 (often 'propitiation' or 'sacrifice of atonement'), because Cyril's argument rests on Paul using the same word as Exodus; ἱλασμός (1 John 2:2) is 'propitiation' and ἵλεως 'gracious' to keep the word family visible.

rejected: the man who came to be
choices.why: 'He who became man for our sake' (τὸν δι' ἡμᾶς γενόμενον ἄνθρωπον): kept as 'became man', not 'the man who came to be', which would misstate Cyril's Christology.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-quotation of Matthew 13:43 begun at the end of s6. Cyril's text has κατὰ καιρούς ('in due time'), which is not in Matthew 13:43; rendered as he quotes it. Ends mid-quotation of John 14:6 ('Οὐδεὶς ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸν | Πατέρα'); s8 carries the citation where the quotation closes, and 'I am the way' here is already cited to John 14:6. Exodus 25:17–22: LXX and English verse numbers agree here. Variants in Cyril's text against Rahlfs LXX: χρυσᾶ τορνευτά ('of wrought/turned gold') for χρυσοτορευτά; ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν ἄνωθεν ('on the top, above') for ἐπὶ τὴν κιβωτὸν ἄνωθεν. Translated as Cyril has them. ἱλαστήριον is rendered 'mercy seat' throughout, including in Romans 3:25 (often 'propitiation' or 'sacrifice of atonement'), because Cyril's argument rests on Paul using the same word as Exodus; ἱλασμός (1 John 2:2) is 'propitiation' and ἵλεως 'gracious' to keep the word family visible. ἐπικειμένη is feminine though ἱλαστήριον is neuter (Migne as printed); sense unaffected. 'He who became man for our sake' (τὸν δι' ἡμᾶς γενόμενον ἄνθρωπον): kept as 'became man', not 'the man who came to be', which would misstate Cyril's Christology. 'Ask, and it will be given to you': Cyril joins John 16:24 to the wording of Matthew 7:7 (identical in Luke 11:9); John 16:24 itself ends 'and you will receive'. 'I am the door': John 10:9 (also 10:7). 'Through him we draw near' may echo Ephesians 2:18 / Hebrews 7:25; doubtful, uncited. The disciples' divine signs may recall Luke 9:1 or Acts 1:8; doubtful, uncited. ἁγιασμός rendered 'sanctification' (not 'holiness'); ὑπεροχή 'supreme excellence'.
